Training

A structured doctoral programme at the interface of disciplines and sectors.

Our training philosophy

The Met2Adapt training programme combines cutting-edge research projects with a comprehensive curriculum of scientific, technical and transferable skills. To this end, Met2Adapt brings together a team of world-leading academic and industrial experts and puts in place an innovation-driven training programme. Our overarching aim is to deliver highly qualified individuals with a multidisciplinary skillset across the spectrum of meta-materials and structural engineering, renewable energy production, computer programming, and the modelling of life-cycle impacts in the energy sector. They will be able to drive forward the long-overdue integration of advanced materials in renewable energy production. Key to our training methodology is our firm commitment to an active, student-centred ‘training by research’ environment, which puts the Doctoral Candidates in charge of their training.

The training programme

High-level research and supervision

A holistic training experience with state-of-the-art laboratory facilities, hands-on technical training and expert scientific supervision across all host institutions.

Personal Career Development Plan

Each Doctoral Candidate co-designs a Personal Career Development Plan (PCDP), calibrated to their scientific strengths and long-term professional aspirations.

What it includes
  • Enrolment in the doctoral school of the host institution.
  • Formal training activities targeting transferable skills.
  • Structured progress monitoring and strategic mentoring sessions, to stay aligned with project objectives and address research challenges early.

Gender balance and inclusion

Gender balance and inclusiveness are actively promoted throughout the Met2Adapt programme.

How we put it into practice
  • Expert-led workshops on inclusive leadership, cultural competency and recognising implicit bias, as part of the core training modules.
  • An Equal Opportunities Officer monitors diversity metrics, from the applicant pool to DC retention and satisfaction, and feeds the results back into our strategies.
  • Flexible working arrangements: parental leave, childcare responsibilities and part-time options are respected and supported without penalising career progression or publication output.

Thematic Training Weeks

Network-wide events organised by the beneficiaries, where all Met2Adapt scholars and associated partners work directly with the Doctoral Candidates through lectures, personal tutorials and workshop-style sessions.

8 core training weeks, open to all Doctoral Candidates, from April 2027 to the end of the project. Dates marked TBC are provisional.

    1

    Training Week 1

    Introduction Week

    Research methods, scientific writing, literature review, project management, environmental sustainability and green measures, conflict resolution, research data management and open science, ethics in research, responsible AI.

    ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland

  2. July 2027TBC
    2

    Training Week 2

    Fundamentals and design principles of meta-materials and meta-structures for wave conditioning and vibration mitigation

    Fundamental concepts, structural instabilities, variable length structures and nonlinear meta-structures; modelling tools; experimental techniques for metamaterial response characterisation; application in critical infrastructure.

    University of Bologna, Bologna, Italy

  3. November 2027TBC

    Training Week 3

    Adaptability and resilience against climate change: challenges and digital opportunities for the European industry

    Life cycle of onshore and offshore wind turbines, climatic hazards, life cycle analysis of sensitive environments employing meta-materials.

    Technical University of Denmark, Kongens Lyngby, Denmark

  4. January 2028TBC
    4

    Structural Health Monitoring and prognostics for meta-materials

    SHM, sensor development, artificial intelligence and prognosis, laboratory experiments, design and calculation methods, latest trends in vibration mitigation.

    ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland

    The ocean environment; assessment of wind and ocean resources; design of ocean energy conversion devices and shore protection systems; meta-materials and meta-structures for shallow-water control.
